title: api: schema versioning for request/response deprecations + beta headers + backcompat shims
author: Evan Chen
description: Motivation: standardize how we evolve the API surface (requests/responses) across streaming, function/tool calling, and structured output while preserving OpenAI-compatibility. This change introduces a lightweight schema versioning header (X-Redwood-API-Version) and a beta flag header (X-Redwood-API-Beta) that callers can opt-in to. It also implements backward-compatibility shims in the OpenAI compatibility layer to translate legacy request shapes to the new canonical schema and emit deprecation warnings. Scope: server-side request/response validation, compatibility layer translation, streaming frame stability fixes, function/tool-calling param normalization, structured-output contract enforcement, SDK compatibility notes. Rollout plan: feature-flagged on production with gradual rollout by region and traffic percentage; telemetry aggregated for each version and beta header; deprecation period of 90 days for legacy fields with clear warning headers. Backwards compatibility: we add per-request shim translations for the most common legacy shapes (e.g., old "tools" arrays, legacy "stream_event" frames) and return X-Redwood-Deprecation header when a legacy shape was used. Clients are encouraged to switch to the new canonical shapes and to include X-Redwood-API-Version in future requests. Testing: unit tests for translation logic, integration tests for streaming frames and function calling, e2e tests against redwood-openai-compat to ensure no regressions. Related linear tickets: ENG-4213, ENG-4378, ENG-4402. This description contains the implementation summary, compatibility commitments, and rollout steps.
commits_summary: feat(api): add X-Redwood-API-Version and X-Redwood-API-Beta headers and server-side parsing
feat(compat): implement backcompat shims in redwood-openai-compat for legacy tool/function shapes
fix(streaming): stabilize streaming frame parsing and fix edge-case with partial delta frames
feat(schema): introduce canonical request/response schema and validation layer
test: add unit/integration tests and e2e scenarios for schema translation
docs: document new headers, deprecation policy, and SDK migration guide
chore: add telemetry hooks and deprecation metrics
review_comments_summary: Priya Nair: Can we make the beta header optional by default and only set it in SDKs when opted in? Author: yes, beta header is opt-in; feature flags control server enforcement.
Marco Li: The streaming frame fix LGTM but please add a regression test for the partial delta case. Author: added test in test_frame_shims.py and included an e2e scenario.
Samira Khan: Are we emitting deprecation telemetry for both request and response shapes? Author: telemetry hooks added for request translation occurrences and also on server-side response downgrades.
QA: E2E tests passed for Python and TS SDKs against compat layer. Small race observed when closing streams fast; mitigated by short backoff in parser. Author: applied parser backoff and retried CI.
Security: small review of header parsing to avoid injection; code uses strict header tokenization. Author: confirmed and added additional unit tests.
Product: confirm 90-day deprecation window and rollback plan. Author: documented rollback and region-by-region rollback flags in rollout/flags.yaml.
release_notes: Introduce X-Redwood-API-Version and X-Redwood-API-Beta headers for schema versioning. Backcompat shims added to redwood-openai-compat to allow legacy request shapes during a 90-day deprecation window. Streaming stability fixes and function/tool calling normalization. See docs for migration steps.
merge_summary: Merged via squash on 2026-02-26 after green CI. Rollout gated by feature flags and disabled by default. Telemetry shows initial translations <0.5% of traffic before staged rollout. SDK patch releases published to document headers and opt-in behavior.
